t: A mobile concrete pump (mobile plant) insured with IMT 55 causes damage to an underground water pipe while in operation at a site. Under IMT 55 the liability for the pipe is
o: excluded, as damage to pipes or cables arising out of operation as a tool of trade is specifically excluded
covered under Section II up to Rs 7.5 lakh
e: IMT 55 (mobile plant - all other cases) excludes liability for subsidence, flooding or water pollution and damage to pipes or cables arising from operation as a tool of trade, as well as explosion of pressure vessels except as required by the MV Act.

t: A truck insured with IMT 56 (trailers - road transit) tows a loaded trailer; in an accident the goods on the trailer are destroyed. The insurer is
o: not liable for damage to property conveyed by the towed vehicle
liable under Section I for the goods
liable under Section II up to Rs 7.5 lakh
liable if the goods belonged to the insured
e: IMT 56 extends Sections I and II to a vehicle attached for towing but excludes damage to property conveyed by the towed vehicle, and any loss while towing more vehicles than permitted by law.

t: IMT 57 is used to adapt the standard Motor Trade policy for
o: motorised two wheelers bearing a trade certificate, substituting 'Motorised Two Wheeler' for 'Motor Vehicle'
vintage cars held by a dealer
e: IMT 57 (Motorised Two Wheelers - Motor Trade only) substitutes item 5 of the schedule to cover any motorised two wheeler (with sidecar) in the insured's custody bearing the stated trade certificate number.

t: Under IMT 58 a dealer who lends courtesy cars to customers whose vehicles are under repair must
o: restrict loans to 7 days per customer
record each loan in a register and submit a statement of the days each vehicle was in use within one month of expiry, premium being adjustable
insure each courtesy car under a separate private car policy
obtain a cover note for each loan
e: IMT 58 allows loan or hire of vehicles to customers whose vehicles are under repair, subject to a register of loans (date, make, registered/chassis number, duration) and a statement within one month of expiry, with premium adjustment at expiry.

t: IMT 59 extends a motor trade policy to use of a vehicle by the insured, a member, director or employee of the insured for
e: IMT 59 (private use by member/director/employee) makes the policy operative for social, domestic or pleasure use, treating such person as the insured for Section II provided he is not indemnified elsewhere and has not been refused insurance.

t: Under IMT 60 (demonstration driving extension) a prospective customer may drive a dealer's vehicle provided he
o: is a named driver in the policy
has deposited the vehicle's IDV as security
drives with the insured's permission and is accompanied by the insured or a person in the insured's employment
e: IMT 60 covers demonstration driving by persons not in the insured's employment, with the insured's permission, accompanied by the insured or his employee; Class F allows this within 80 km of the insured's address.

t: IMT 61 (tuition - driving extension) can be attached only to motor trade policies issued
o: on named driver basis, and the learner must be accompanied by a named driver mentioned in the schedule
e: IMT 61 applies only to motor trade policies on named driver basis and covers demonstration or tuition by any other person driving with the insured's permission accompanied by a named driver in the schedule.

t: The own damage premium of a car before NCB is Rs 18,000 and the insured has three consecutive claim-free years. The NCB amount is
e: ★ Key fact (repeated across the mocks of this paper). GR 27: NCB for three consecutive claim-free years is 35%; 35% of Rs 18,000 = Rs 6,300, leaving a net OD premium of Rs 11,700.

t: Under IMT 62, the additional premium for deleting the 50% limitation on tyres under a Motor Trade Road Transit policy may be charged as
o: 0.5% of IDV subject to a minimum of Rs 100
1% of basic OD premium or Rs 5 per chassis/vehicle per trip, provided the manufacturer/dealer has insurable interest
e: IMT 62 deletes the words limiting tyre liability to 50% of replacement cost from proviso (b) of Section I; the trainer's notes give the premium as 1% (of basic OD premium) or Rs 5 per chassis/vehicle per trip for brand new vehicles with new tyres.

t: When IMT 63 is attached to a Motor Trade Internal Risks policy,
o: Section I is cancelled and the insurer is not liable for damage to the motor vehicle or its accessories, cover being restricted to liability risks
the policy is extended to cover work away from premises
the deductible is reduced to nil
e: IMT 63 (restriction of cover to liability risks only) cancels Section I and the vehicle-damage parts of Section II(2), so the insurer is not liable for damage to the motor vehicle or its accessories; the notes mention a property damage limit of Rs 1.5 lakh per accident.

t: Under IMT 65 (work away from premises) for an Internal Risks policy, the additional premium is
o: 0.065% on total wages subject to a minimum of Rs 50, excluding injury or damage from driving in a public place
e: IMT 65 deems the premises to include places where the insured performs work, at 0.065% on total wages (minimum Rs 50), but excludes injury or damage resulting from driving the vehicle in a public place; IMT 64 covers open-air car parks with 50% of area reckoned.

t: Depreciation applicable to nylon and plastic parts in a partial loss claim, irrespective of the age of the vehicle, is
e: GR 9 schedule: all rubber, nylon, plastic parts, tyres, tubes, batteries and airbags 50%; fibre glass 30%; glass nil; other parts as per the age-based table.

t: For transfer of a package policy in the transferee's name under GR 17, the insurer requires
o: an NOC from the transferor and nothing else
only the transferee's letter of request
payment of the full premium afresh
acceptable evidence of sale, a fresh proposal form, surrender of the old certificate of insurance and a fee of Rs 50
e: GR 17: transfer of the OD section requires a specific request from the transferee with the transferor's consent, acceptable evidence of sale, a fresh proposal form, surrender of the old certificate and Rs 50 for the fresh certificate; NCB is adjusted to the transferee's entitlement.

t: A car bought on hire purchase is to be insured. Under GR 19 the policy and certificate are issued
o: in the name of the hirer only, the owner's interest being protected by IMT 5
in the name of the owner (financier) only
in the name of the hirer with the owner as co-insured
in the joint names of hirer and owner
e: GR 19: policies and certificates under hire purchase are issued in the hirer's name only; issuance in joint names is prohibited and the owner's interest is protected by IMT 5 (lease: lessee only with IMT 6; hypothecation: registered owner with IMT 7).

t: A car is hypothecated to a bank. Under GR 21 the policy is issued
o: in the name of the owner with the bank as loss payee under IMT 5
in the name of the registered owner only, with IMT 7 protecting the bank's interest
in the joint names of the owner and the bank
in the name of the bank only
e: GR 21: for hypothecation agreements the policy is issued only in the registered owner's name - joint names are prohibited - and the pledgee's interest is protected by IMT 7.

t: A private car package policy is extended under IMT 31 for a rally lasting 4 days. The additional premium is
e: ★ Key fact (repeated across the mocks of this paper). Rally extension for private car package policies: Rs 60 for the first day and Rs 30 for each succeeding day: 60 + 3 x 30 = Rs 150 (liability only policies: Rs 25 and Rs 15).

t: A car came with a factory-fitted CNG kit whose value cannot be ascertained. Under GR 42 the insurer charges
o: Rs 60 under OD and nothing under liability
4% on an estimated kit value and Rs 60 under liability
no extra OD premium for the kit, but Rs 60 under the liability section
e: GR 42: a bi-fuel kit is insured at 4% of its declared value; if it came with the vehicle and its value cannot be ascertained no extra OD premium is chargeable, but Rs 60 towards liability cover on account of the CNG/LPG system is charged even for inbuilt kits.

t: A fire and/or theft only policy under GR 45A (without liability cover) may be issued only when
o: the insured specifically requests in writing that the vehicle will not be used at all during the entire policy period
the vehicle is more than 10 years old
the insured has a Liability Only policy with another insurer
the vehicle is a commercial vehicle under Class D
e: GR 45A permits fire and/or theft only cover at the specific written request of the insured that during the entire policy period the vehicle will not be used at all; it is prohibited for Classes D, E, F and G.

t: A car was laid up for three months during the policy year and a lay-up rebate was allowed. At renewal the NCB is computed
o: on the full renewal premium ignoring the rebate
on the renewal premium after deducting the rebate for the laid-up period
e: GR 27 / IMT 11A: NCB is to be calculated on the next renewal premium after deduction of the lay-up rebate; NCB is allowed only where the vehicle was continuously insured for 12 months without a claim.

t: Under a Class F Road Risks policy, the demonstration driving extension can be given for a distance up to
o: 80 km from the address of the insured
120 km from the address of the insured
160 km from the address of the insured
e: Class F special features: demonstration-driving extension up to 80 km from the insured's address; the geographical area for new vehicles can be extended to 120 km on extra premium using IMT 41.

t: For a Class G Internal Risks liability only policy (area not exceeding 2000 sq m) the premium is
e: Class G: package premium is 0.28% on wages plus Rs 150; liability only is 0.28% on wages; for area exceeding 2000 sq m, Rs 15 (package) or Rs 8 (liability) is added per 1000 sq m or part thereof.

t: Under Rule 34 of CMVR, a dealer who handles both motorcycles and heavy goods vehicles must
o: make separate applications for trade certificates for each class of vehicle
obtain a certificate only for the heavier class
obtain a single composite trade certificate
e: Rule 34 requires separate applications for trade certificates for each class - motorcycle, invalid carriage, LMV, MPM, MGV, HPM, HGV and any other vehicle.

t: IMT 49 attached to a mobile plant policy excludes
o: liability to the public arising out of operation of the vehicle or attached plant as a tool of trade, except as required by the MV Act
fire and theft while laid up
e: IMT 49 (exclusion of liability to the public - working risk) and IMT 52 (exclusion while in use as a tool of trade) remove Section II liability arising from tool-of-trade operation except so far as necessary to meet MV Act requirements.

t: A claim is paid for damage to a trailer insured along with its hauling truck under one policy. The effect on NCB is
o: no effect, as trailers have no NCB
NCB is reduced by one slab
only the trailer portion loses NCB
NCB of the entire policy is affected
e: A claim made either on the trailer or on the hauling vehicle affects the NCB of the entire policy; also no lay-up concession is permissible for trailers.

t: A three wheeler specially designed for operation by a physically handicapped person is rated as
o: a commercial three wheeler under C-1
a two wheeler with side car
e: The two wheeler tariff provides that a three wheeler designed for operation by physically handicapped persons is rated as a two wheeler with side car (25% OD discount for side car).

t: A claim for theft of parts and accessories from a car (vehicle not stolen) may be settled
o: only if the vehicle is also stolen
without any FIR for amounts below Rs 25,000
on production of bills/cash memos without waiting for the final police report, subject to FIR or case diary and a letter of indemnity and subrogation
only after the final police investigation report
e: Theft of accessories and parts may be settled on bills without waiting for the final police report, subject to FIR/case diary; for claims above Rs 5,000 a surveyor may be appointed and a letter of indemnity and subrogation is obtained before settlement.

t: In a dealer tie-up (cashless) OD claim, the repair estimate is prepared by
o: the dealer, who also intimates the claim in the insurer's system
e: Tie-up flow: intimation to dealer, policy validation and claim intimation by the dealer, claim form, estimate prepared by the dealer, online survey appointment, survey, record verification and liability confirmation by the surveyor, bills and satisfaction note, approval and NEFT to the dealer.

t: The minimum value for premium computation of a four wheeled passenger vehicle with carrying capacity of 12 passengers is
e: ★ Key fact (repeated across the mocks of this paper). Four wheeled passenger vehicles carrying more than 6 but not more than 17 passengers have a minimum IDV of Rs 20,000; the corresponding three wheelers have Rs 25,000; 17-36 passengers Rs 30,000.

t: According to the OD claim checklist, where third party injury or property damage is also involved the insured should
o: settle with the third party directly
wait for the surveyor before informing anyone
inform the police about the accident and note names and addresses of witnesses
e: The checklist requires the insured to inform the police if TP injury/property damage is involved, note witness details, inform the insurer immediately quoting the policy number, obtain and submit the claim form and estimate.

t: After completion of repairs under an OD claim, the insured has to sign and submit to the repairer
o: a discharge voucher for the IDV
e: The checklist states that after repairs are over the insured signs a satisfaction certificate and submits it to the repairers; in tie-up claims the satisfaction note accompanies the bill.

t: In every claim settled on total loss basis, the policy is
o: continued till expiry for the replacement vehicle
cancelled with effect from the date of loss without any refund of premium
e: In all total loss claims (actual total loss, net of salvage, or theft) the policy is cancelled w.e.f. the date of loss without refund of premium, and the RTO is informed.

t: The documents to be verified for an OD claim on a goods carrying vehicle, in addition to the RC and driving licence, are
o: PAN card and Aadhaar of the owner
fitness certificate, road permit/tax details, load challan and trip sheet
e: Documents for commercial vehicle OD claims: DL, RC, fitness certificate, load challan, road permit/tax details and trip sheet; for private cars and two wheelers only DL and RC.

t: The minimum value for premium computation of a three wheeled passenger vehicle (up to 6 passengers) not exceeding 150 cc is
e: Three wheelers with capacity not exceeding 6 passengers: not exceeding 150 cc Rs 1,500; 150-250 cc Rs 2,500; exceeding 250 cc Rs 4,000.

t: Personal accident cover under GR 36 (compulsory or optional) is NOT available under
o: Motor Trade policies of Classes E, F and G
e: GR 36 (PA cover under motor policy) is not applicable to Classes E, F and G; motor trade policies carry no CPA and no NCB.

t: For a brand new private car the bundled policy combines one year OD with third party cover for
e: Bundled policies for new vehicles: 1 year OD + 3 years TP for private cars (1+3) and 1 year OD + 5 years TP for two wheelers (1+5); standalone OD and standalone CPA policies are also available.

t: A 'maxicab' under the MV Act is a vehicle constructed or adapted to carry for hire or reward
o: not more than 6 passengers excluding the driver
more than 6 passengers but not more than 12 passengers excluding the driver
e: A motorcab carries not more than 6 passengers excluding the driver; a maxicab carries more than 6 but not more than 12 passengers excluding the driver, for hire or reward.

t: The principle that allows an insurer who has paid a claim to step into the insured's shoes and recover from a liable third party is:
e: ★ Core fact (asked across III papers). Subrogation is a corollary of indemnity; it does not apply to life or personal accident (benefit) policies.

t: A two wheeler aged 2 years 1 month is damaged. Assessment before depreciation: plastic cowl Rs 3,000, metal parts Rs 4,000, tyre Rs 2,000 (vehicle also damaged), labour Rs 1,500. The amount payable is
e: Plastic 50% = Rs 1,500; metal 15% (2-3 years) = Rs 3,400; tyre 50% = Rs 1,000; labour Rs 1,500; total Rs 7,400 less compulsory deductible Rs 100 = Rs 7,300.

t: A private car (1800 cc) with IDV Rs 7,50,000 has an assessed loss of Rs 5,80,000. The insured wishes to retain the wreck, valued at Rs 1,20,000. The claim payable is
e: Rs 5,80,000 is 77% of IDV, so the claim is a total loss settled net of salvage: Rs 7,50,000 - Rs 1,20,000 - compulsory deductible Rs 2,000 = Rs 6,28,000.

t: A 17,000 kg GVW truck aged 9 years carries IMT 23. Damage: metal bumper Rs 10,000, metal cabin parts Rs 60,000, labour Rs 20,000. The claim payable is
e: Bumper (IMT 23 item): 40% depreciation (5-10 years) gives Rs 6,000, then 50% borne by insured = Rs 3,000. Cabin parts 40% = Rs 36,000. Labour Rs 20,000. Total Rs 59,000 less deductible Rs 1,500 (GVW exceeding 16,500 kg) = Rs 57,500.

t: An ambulance (Class D) with IDV Rs 20 lakh suffers a loss assessed at Rs 1,50,000 after depreciation; no salvage. The amount payable is
e: Ambulances are rated under Class D, where the compulsory deductible is 0.5% of IDV subject to a minimum of Rs 2,000: 0.5% of Rs 20,00,000 = Rs 10,000; Rs 1,50,000 - Rs 10,000 = Rs 1,40,000.

t: A car aged 4 years 10 months has a current listed selling price of Rs 6,00,000. Its IDV under the GR 8 schedule is
e: GR 8: 4 to 5 years - 50% depreciation; Rs 6,00,000 x 50% = Rs 3,00,000. Beyond 5 years IDV is by mutual agreement.

t: The gross OD premium of a car is Rs 24,000 and the insured has four consecutive claim-free years. The net OD premium after NCB is
e: NCB for four consecutive claim-free years is 45%: Rs 24,000 x 55% = Rs 13,200.

t: A car is insured with two different insurers; the later policy (annual premium Rs 6,000) is cancelled under GR 24 after running 73 days of 365 with no claim. The refund is
e: In double insurance with different insurers the later policy is cancelled with pro-rata refund: Rs 6,000 x 292/365 = Rs 4,800.

t: A goods carrier is also used for the owner's private purposes. The CVT premium is Rs 30,000. The premium chargeable with IMT 34 is
e: Vehicles designed as commercial vehicles and used for both commercial and private purposes (not hire or reward) are charged the CVT rate with a 25% loading: Rs 30,000 x 1.25 = Rs 37,500.

t: In a life insurance contract, insurable interest must exist:
o: At the time of the claim only
Both at inception and at claim
e: ★ Core fact (asked across III papers). Life: at inception only. Marine: at the time of loss. Fire and motor: at both inception and loss.

t: A dealer's Class G package premium on wages works out to Rs 8,000 for premises of 3,500 sq m. The additional premium for area exceeding 2,000 sq m is
e: For superficial area exceeding 2000 sq m, Rs 15 (package) or Rs 8 (liability only) is charged for every 1000 sq m or part thereof: excess 1,500 sq m = 2 units x Rs 15 = Rs 30.

t: A driving school car has an applicable OD premium of Rs 10,000. Under GR 44 the OD premium chargeable is
e: GR 44: vehicles with double clutches and brakes used for driving tuition by an RTA-recognised school are charged the OD premium plus 60% loading: Rs 16,000; liability premium is as per tariff.

t: A two wheeler owner declares accessories worth Rs 1,200 for theft cover under IMT 33. The additional premium is
e: IMT 33: 3% of the value of accessories subject to a minimum of Rs 50; 3% of Rs 1,200 = Rs 36, so the minimum Rs 50 applies.

t: A truck owner takes IMT 17 PA cover for his paid driver and cleaner with a CSI of Rs 1,00,000 each. The additional premium is
e: GR 36B rate for commercial vehicles is Rs 6 per Rs 10,000 CSI: Rs 60 per person for Rs 1 lakh; for two persons Rs 120.
